en Español

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
700 AM EST Fri Nov 20 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Offshore of the Southeast U.S. Coast:
Surface observations indicate that a broad low pressure area is now
located near the east coast of central Florida.  The low is 
currently producing disorganized showers and thunderstorms extending 
from the central Florida peninsula east-southeastward over the 
Atlantic. This system could acquire subtropical or tropical 
characteristics while it moves generally northward to 
north-northeastward near or just offshore of the southeastern United 
States coast through the weekend.

Regardless of subtropical or tropical development, the system is 
expected to produce strong gusty winds, dangerous surf, rip 
currents and coastal flooding along portions of the southeast and 
mid-Atlantic U.S. coasts into early next week.  In addition, heavy 
rainfall and the threat of flash flooding will continue across 
portions of the Florida peninsula today, potentially spreading 
northward toward coastal portions of the Carolinas and the 
mid-Atlantic over the weekend.  Interests along the eastern coast 
of the United States should continue to monitor the progress of 
this system.  Additional information on this system, including Gale 
Warnings, can be found in High Seas Forecasts issued by the National 
Weather Service, as well as products issued by your local National 
Weather Service forecast office.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...30 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...50 percent.

&&
High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service can be 
found under AWIPS header NFDHSFAT1, WMO header FZNT01 KWBC, and 
online at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFAT1.php
